items.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: And this guy named Ray Burns, he saw me down there. And he says, “Jimmy, I heard you on one of these records down here, you’re playing the Fender.” I says, “yeah.” He said, “well you got a pencil and paper?”

ctx.x: Yeah. I worked with King Curtis for seven years. Formed a solid band, everything. But then I would go downtown and they’d call me for a record date and all. So I had to start playing the Fender bass. I had a different style from all the guys on the Fender bass — my own creation. But it worked out nice for me. So the first week I went down I think I made about three sessions, and I got seven hundred and something dollars. So I said now wait a minute — there’s money in this thing. I wonder if I can keep it going.…
all my bass lines. So then it comes time to record this Broadway show. So we recorded it. And the thing was a hit.
